findings.failure_path: may_write_from_bash() returns False when len(command) > 65536, and handle() then returns base without calling bash_write_targets. Before this change, every Bash command was normalized. Now a write such as `rm skills/x/SKILL.md; : <64 KiB of padding>` skips the shared-skill checkpoint (bypass by omission). The 64 KiB bound was copied from owner-dispatch.sh, but there exceeding it forces the full path. Here it skips the gate. No test exercises an oversized command.
findings.smallest_fix: Return True (load the normalizer) when len(command) > 65536. Return False only when the input is not a string or is empty. Add a test with a padded write command over 64 KiB.

findings.failure_path: The new `*) continue` arm stops every git subcommand except push/merge/pull from reaching the original second `case "$sub"` dispatch. If that dispatch had arms for other subcommands that update the default branch (for example rebase, reset, update-ref, branch -f, or commit), those arms can no longer run, so their denies are skipped. The packet shows only the push arm, so I can't confirm this. The new tests cover only quiet commands and push/merge.
findings.smallest_fix: Add every subcommand arm from the original second case to the `push|merge|pull` lazy-load arm, or replace `*) continue` with a fall-through that calls ensure_base_git_context. Add a test asserting the same verdicts as before for every arm that existed.

concern_results.conclusion: I found one credible fast-path bypass. skill-loading.py may_write_from_bash() returns False for any command longer than 65536 characters. Returning False skips the write checkpoint, so it fails open instead of closed. I found one evidence gap: in guard-merge-authorization.sh, the new `*) continue` arm stops every git subcommand except push/merge/pull from reaching the original second case. The packet does not show whether that case had other arms. The other paths I checked fail closed: owner-dispatch's backslash/[Ee]dit/[Ww]rite/apply_patch guard, the R0 stamp's 0700/-O/symlink checks, the waived-path registration that runs before the prefilter, and the nested-export toplevel realpath check.

The size-bounded fast path in skill-loading.py is the opposite of owner-dispatch.sh's bound. owner-dispatch falls back to the full jq path above 64 KiB. skill-loading skips the full path above 64 KiB, and no test covers an oversized write command. Everything else I checked keeps fail-closed behavior on the diffed paths.
